about.title: Commerce Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Commerce sits along one of the busiest freight and commuter corridors in Los Angeles County, with I-5 and Telegraph Road carrying heavy volumes of cars and trucks through the city every day. Public crash records show 254 injury collisions in the most recent final year, with 333 people hurt and 2 lives lost — and Friday afternoons between 4 and 6 p.m. tend to see the most reported incidents. If you were injured in one of these crashes, the moments right after matter: photos, witness names, and medical records can quietly disappear or get harder to obtain the longer you wait. LawProactive doesn't practice law — we're a free connection service that puts you in touch with an independent personal injury attorney familiar with Commerce and the surrounding LA County courts. There's no upfront cost, and no obligation to move forward. The goal is simple: get you talking to someone who can look at your situation before the insurance company gets ahead of you.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before the Insurer Calls

items.title: California Gives You Two Years — Sometimes Less
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a claim, but if a government vehicle or road defect was involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months. An attorney can tell you quickly which clock applies to your case.

items.title: Comparative Fault Won't Erase Your Claim
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, meaning you can still recover damages even if you're partly at fault — your share of responsibility just reduces the amount. Insurers know this and often try to shift blame onto you early, before you've spoken with anyone.

items.title: Recorded Statements Can Undercut You Later
items.desc: There's no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering under California law, but a careless answer in a recorded statement to the other driver's insurer can be used to argue your injuries are less serious than they are. It's worth having someone review your case before you say anything on record.

items.question: I was in a crash near the I-5 and Telegraph Road area — what should I do first?
items.answer: Get medical attention even if you feel okay, since some injuries show up hours or days later. Try to document the scene with photos and get contact information for any witnesses, and avoid giving a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company until you've spoken with an attorney. LawProactive can connect you with someone familiar with crashes reported along that corridor.

items.question: What if the accident happened on a city street or involved a city vehicle?
items.answer: Claims involving a government entity, like a city-owned vehicle or a defect in a public road, often come with a much shorter filing deadline — sometimes just six months instead of two years. Missing that window can end your claim before it starts, so it's important to get this looked at quickly. An independent attorney can help determine whether a government claim applies to your situation.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything for connecting me with an attorney?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service, and we don't charge you to connect you with an independent personal injury attorney. Attorneys in the network typically work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if you recover compensation. There's no obligation to hire anyone after speaking with them.
